correctness.rationale: For every n>=2 the directed de Bruijn-type overlap graph has one directed edge per length-n binary word of Hamming weight 1 or 2 and vertices of length n-1 with weights 0,1,2. Weight-0 and weight-2 vertices have forced outgoing edges; weight-1 states have two. A cyclic universal word corresponds bijectively to an edge-distinct Euler tour normalized at the unique root edge 0^(n-1)1. BEST gives the number as the in-arborescence count. At weight-1 index i, append-0 moves to i+1 (or root) and append-1 then forced shifts moves to n-2-i; an upper-half append-one creates a closed interval away from root, so is forbidden. Every independent lower-half choice strictly increases the index until root and is valid. Exactly floor((n-1)/2) independent choices yield 2^floor((n-1)/2); all lengths n>=2 and rotation primitivity covered. Independent exact root-Laplacian cofactors n=2..8 reproduce counts and edge totals; all-n follows from forest bijection.

evidence: BEST/the matrix-tree theorem already give a general determinant expression for arbitrary Eulerian overlap graphs, but a determinant is not the evaluated all-n 2-power formula; the proof resolves the family-specific arborescence structure.

originality.rationale: Ruskey-Sawada-Williams and Sawada-Williams-Wong establish existence and construction of fixed/weight-range Ucycles. Sawada-Gabric 2025 develops sampling via Eulerian arborescences and has small examples (including n=3). The full all-n closed count and classification of forced/free arborescence choices are not in primary material inspected; a small case count is known and explicitly not claimed new.
residual_risks: Classical BEST theorem and matrix-tree theorem make counts algorithmically accessible; a prior direct cofactor evaluation for precisely weights 1/2 may already give the closed formula.
The Sawada-Gabric 2025 paper includes random tree selection and examples, so known methodology and small cases must not be misrepresented as original.
